text: 🇲🇽✊ Dengue down 84% in two years — without privatizing public health. At Tuesday's health briefing, Health Secretary David Kershenobich presented the numbers: • 2024: 13,398 confirmed cases • 2025: 3,511 confirmed cases • 2026 so far: 2,136 cases, 4 deaths The strategy: the "5 steps for a mosquito-free home" community campaign plus Wolbachia-bacteria mosquito deployment in Yucatán and other states. Yucatán is down to 9 cases this year. — Dr. David Kershenobich, Health Secretary Public science. Public health. Public results.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 Mexico and Uruguay send food to Cuba — against a 60-year blockade. Sheinbaum confirmed at the podium that Mexico recently coordinated another humanitarian shipment to Cuba, with Uruguay joining. "Recently we sent food and supplies, and Uruguay participated. This is part of Mexico's commitment to the Cuban people — and to the principle that no people should be suffocated by a blockade." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on Cuba solidarity Mexico has voted against the US embargo at the UN every year. While Washington tightens sanctions, the region answers with rice, milk, and medicine.

🇲🇽✊ Free, public, and now stamped on the box. Sheinbaum announced that every medicine bought by the Mexican government in the next consolidated purchase will arrive with a printed label: property of the public health sector, free of charge. "It's not promotion. It's a measure to inhibit theft and resale in private pharmacies. People should know this was purchased with public resources and delivered free." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on stopping medicine theft Cofepris is already pursuing criminal complaints and pharmacy shutdowns. Public medicine stays public.

🇲🇽✊ "I don't believe teachers generated the provocation." After yesterday's CNTE march in Mexico City ended with clashes, opposition outlets rushed to blame the teachers. Sheinbaum refused the frame. "There was a lot of provocation yesterday. Honestly, I don't believe it was teachers who generated it. Dialogue with the CNTE continues — we will always privilege dialogue with every expression of the teaching profession." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on the teachers' mobilization A government that doesn't criminalize protest. The talks with CNTE remain open.

🇲🇽🛢️ Pemex and Petrobras: South-South energy sovereignty, signed this month. Sheinbaum confirmed the cooperation agreement between Mexico's Pemex and Brazil's Petrobras will be signed in June — covering deep-water and shallow-water exploration, with Brazilian technology transferred to revive Mexican production. "Brazilian technology is among the most advanced in the world. Petrobras has developed mechanisms that let us identify deeper reserves and re-analyze already-exploited fields." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Pemex–Petrobras pact Two state-owned oil companies, two governments that won't privatize their subsoil. The energy alternative to Washington isn't theoretical — it's a signature away.

🔥🇲🇽 "Bringing a Spanish deputy to lecture us about sovereignty is Kafkaesque." Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo — deputy from Spain's far-right Partido Popular — flew to Mexico for a Grupo Salinas event and declared that neither Hernán Cortés nor Isabella the Catholic ever violated Mexican sovereignty. Sheinbaum, at the podium: "They brought in another Spanish deputy — apparently these are the new cadres of Mexican politics. Having to import her to talk about national sovereignty is a bit Kafkaesque." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Mexican right's foreign imports

🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico's affairs are for Mexicans to decide." After US Ambassador Ronald Johnson publicly told the Mexican government to take "politics" out of the cartel fight, Sheinbaum drew the line at the podium. "Ambassadors must be respectful of the internal political affairs of countries. Our ambassador in the United States, in France, or anywhere in the world does not opine on the political affairs of those countries." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on Ronald Johnson Mexico's Constitution enshrines self-determination and non-intervention. Cooperation, yes — instructions from foreign envoys, no.
